changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`

- names `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Both marketplace chunks were held by CHUNK CO-TENANCY, not by any import of the page: rolldown had parked `components/SuggestedBindingsPanel.tsx` (statically imported by the eager `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) in the first, and `console/marketplace/InstalledListWidget.tsx` (bare-imported by the package barrel for its SDUI registration) in the second. An `app-shell-eager-leaves` group in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` isolates those co-tenants so the three declared-lazy pages chunk by their own dynamic-only reachability. The console eager closure moves 3180.2 KB → 3171.5 KB gzipped (−8,888 bytes, 48 → 45 eager chunks) with the three per-chunk ceilings unmoved.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `3a0e7ab05` (merge-base with origin/main): 4 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1778 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2384 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36648790033)

| Main entry chunk (gzip) | 149.5 KB | 350 KB |

| Status | **PASS** | — |

The **eager closure** is every chunk the entry reaches through static imports — what the browser fetches and parses before the app renders. The entry chunk on its own is a small fraction of it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `575bbb6e60437249c51a8c0c22a61e97b05e2527`
Local-runs: none

Read: card objectui#11148 (body, triage comment 5900721690, claim comment 5901098091, dev report comment 5901455875), PR objectui#11157 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the 43 latest check-runs on the head (40 `success`, 3 `skipped`, none in progress once waited to completion), and for context these files at the head through the contents API: `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, `AppNavCanvas.tsx`, `navItemLabel.ts`, `navSurface.ts`, `nav-selection.ts`, `inspectors/AppNavInspector.tsx`, `inspectors/index.ts`, app-shell `package.json` and `src/index.ts`, plus the head tree listing and the base blob of `AppNavCanvas.labelMaps-11128.test.tsx`. Nothing built, run or re-run. Line addresses in the card and the claim were re-read by symbol, not by number, and none is copied here.

Shape: 5 files, +260 / -30, one commit; head repo is the base repo (not a fork); draft, no auto-merge, no assignee; no governed-surface path in the file list.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`renamedLabel` moved verbatim, one copy left — right.** The eight-line body removed from `AppNavCanvas.tsx` and the body added to `navItemLabel.ts` are byte-identical once the `export` keyword is stripped (compared from the diff text). Only the docblock is reworded ("card" to "editor", plus one sentence on why a keystroke-driven editor adds the exact-tag entry once); the key choice — exact tag, else bare language, else a new exact-tag entry — is the one PR objectui#11146 landed. Copies: at the base the helper existed in `AppNavCanvas.tsx` alone (PR objectui#11146's file list adds it to that one file and nowhere else); the diff deletes it there; both editors import the one module (`AppNavCanvas.tsx`: `import { navItemLabelText, renamedLabel } from './navItemLabel.js'`; `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`: `from '../metadata-admin/previews/navItemLabel.js'`). A tree-wide code search is not reachable through this container's proxy, so the reading is the base's one known copy plus the diff, not a grep of every file at the head.

2. **`navItemLabel.ts` is internal — right.** At the head, app-shell's `package.json` `exports` map holds `.` and `./styles.css` only (no new entry), and `src/index.ts` re-exports from `StudioDesignSurface.js` only `StudioDesignSurface` and `StudioDesignSurfaceProps`; it names neither `navItemLabel`, `renamedLabel`, `navItemLabelText` nor `StudioNavItemInspector`. The module ships inside `dist/index.js` as bundled internals, reachable through no published specifier. Nothing publishes.

3. **Display read — right, and inside the card.** `curLabel` is `navItemLabelText(label, locale)` with `locale = useMetadataLocale()` — the same `metadata-admin/i18n.js` hook `AppNavCanvas` calls — and `navItemLabelText` is `resolveI18nLabel(label, locale) ?? ''`: the spec's resolver, in the designer locale, the way the canvas reads it. `title` / `name` are gone from the read (the pin `does not read title / name as the label` renders an item carrying both and asserts an empty textbox). An item with neither `label` nor `title` shows an empty input on both sides: at the base `String(undefined ?? undefined ?? undefined ?? '')` was `''`, at the head `resolveI18nLabel(undefined, locale) ?? ''` is `''`; the placeholder hint and `isPlaceholder` are unchanged for it. The one behaviour change is an item with `title` or `name` but no `label`: at the base the input showed that text and a bind wrote it INTO `label` (an off-spec key copied into the spec key); at the head the input is empty and a bind adopts the object's label. That is the card's **Keys** line applied, so inside the card. The canvas's `navLabel` keeps its `.trim()` and positional fallback over the new helper — the same expression as before, no behaviour change there.

4. **Edit path — right.** The Label input writes `renamedLabel(label, e.target.value, locale)` with `label` the item's own `label` (typed `I18nLabel | undefined`). A string or absent label returns the typed string, so a plain string stays a string (the control pin asserts `'Customers'`). A map returns the map with only the chosen entry replaced: under zh the pin asserts `{ en: 'Accounts', 'zh-CN': '客户账户' }`, so `en` survives. A map without the designer-locale entry gains one on the first keystroke under the exact tag, and every later keystroke finds that entry first — pinned through a stateful harness that feeds each patch back the way `InterfacesPillar` holds the draft, asserting the key list `['en', 'zh-CN']` after each of three keystrokes: exactly one entry, not one per keystroke. Observation, not a finding: the pin titled `writes the en entry the input read, not a second en-US key` runs under locale `en`, where the exact-tag limb matches; the bare-language limb (`en` under `en-US`) is covered by PR objectui#11146's unchanged canvas pins on the same function.

5. **Object-bind site — the implemented rule is right and inside the card; the deviation from the seat's wording is correct.** At the base the bind wrote `isPlaceholder && obj ? obj.label : curLabel`, with `curLabel` a `String(...)` of the label — so binding an object on a map-labelled item wrote `[object Object]` over the whole map, the card's loss through a second door. The seat's Zone-2 wording ("keep curLabel's semantics on the resolved text") read literally keeps `: curLabel` on the new resolved string, which writes a resolved string over a map — the same loss, and the dev's ablation leg A3 is that literal spelling with the bind pin red. Implemented: `isPlaceholder && obj ? renamedLabel(label, obj.label, locale) : label`. Judged case by case: a real plain-string label writes the same string the base wrote (byte-equal); a real map writes the map as authored (the base wrote `[object Object]`); an absent or plain-string placeholder returns `obj.label` through `renamedLabel`, byte-equal to the base; a map placeholder (a map whose resolved text is empty or the new-item sentinel) now sets only the designer locale's entry and keeps the rest. The last case is the card's **Edit** rule applied to the inspector's second write to `label`, and it goes through the one key choice — the dispatch's no-second-copy line is honoured. `isPlaceholder` keeps its expression, now over the resolved text: a map resolving to the sentinel is a placeholder, which the seat asked for. The pin `binding an object keeps a real map label as authored` asserts the map and that the written item still parses under `NavigationItemSchema`.

6. **Pins against the four the direction names — all present.** (i) a map label shows the resolved text under en and under zh: `shows a map label as its en text` / `zh text` assert `Accounts` / `客户` and that no `[object Object]` display value exists; (ii) an edit under zh changes only `zh-CN`: asserted as the whole written map; (iii) a plain string edits as today: the control; (iv) PR objectui#11146's canvas pins unchanged: `AppNavCanvas.labelMaps-11128.test.tsx` is not in the file list and its blob is `4e0baa5cdc…` at both the base and the head — green per the head's Test shards below. The new file renders the real exported `StudioNavItemInspector` under `I18nProvider`, not a copy; the dev's ablation (A1 4 failed, A2 3 failed, A3 1 failed of 8) is their reading and is not re-derived here.

7. **Accept-set and public-surface changes implied by the diff — none.** The label's accepted shape is the spec's `I18nLabel` on both sides; the inspector mishandled a shape the spec already accepted, and now handles it. Dropping the `title` / `name` read removes a consumer-side lenient fallback that the contract never granted (Commandment #0.1), which narrows no accepted set. No export is added to or removed from the package root or its `exports` map; `StudioNavItemInspector` stays a file-level export for tests, as at the base.

8. **Gates on the head — the check-runs' conclusions are the verdicts; none re-run here.** Latest check-runs on `575bbb6e6…`, waited to completion in the foreground: `success` on `Lint`, `Type Check`, `Test (shard 1/8)` through `Test (shard 8/8)`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Test` (the rollup, completed last), `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Overwrite Report`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `README Export Check`, `Pre-Install Import Graph Check`, `Inert vi.mock Specifier Check`, `Shell Escape Residue Scan`, `Action Ref Convention`, `Live E2E (informational)`, the five Doc checks, the three Skill checks and `label`; `skipped` (by the workflows' own conditions, not a red) on `Test (coverage)`, the coverage shard matrix row and `dependabot`. No `failure`, `cancelled` or `timed_out` conclusion on the head. The Test shards being green at the head is what says PR objectui#11146's unchanged canvas pins and the objectui#4881 inspector pins still pass beside the eight new ones.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` — right: no schema, prop, type or accepted set moves; the label's accepted shape is the spec's, unchanged, and the helper move is internal. Changeset `.changeset/11148-nav-inspector-label-map.md` declares `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`, which matches what the diff publishes: a `src/` change to a released package (`@object-ui/app-shell` 17.6.0, `files` includes `dist`) that the presence gate requires a declaration for, a bug fix in a released package, no new published surface (the internal module publishes nothing), no `major` in the fixed group. The changeset body carries the fix's consumer-facing sentence, no model identifier and no line address. Not a `skip-changeset` case. `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Overwrite Report` and `Changeset Claim Re-read` are all `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared. Every deviation and both out-of-scope notes answered:

- **Object-bind deviation** — answered in ① item 5: the implemented rule is right and inside the card; the literal reading of the seat's wording reproduces the defect.
- **PR assignee write not made** — the PR has no assignee at the head while the card's is `os-support-ai`; the dev's permission layer refused the write before it was sent, and the dev stopped rather than re-route, as the role file says. No check-run on the head reads the PR assignee, so it is not a contract finding; the seat surfaces it and mirrors the card's assignee onto the PR as its own act.
- **Labels `tests` and `package: app-shell`** — written by the repo's labeler (`label` check-run, `success`), left as found; not a finding.
- **Line addresses** — the PR body cites by symbol and quoted string, no `path:line`; `Line Citation Gate` is `success`. The card and claim bodies carry addresses of their own; cards are not swept and that is not this diff's finding.
- **Container restart mid-run** — procedural; no bearing on the diff.
- **Out-of-scope (a): the Interfaces pillar's rail crashes on a map-labelled nav item — real at the head, pre-existing, not worsened.** At the head `NavTree` in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` renders `{node.label}` in the group heading and `{node.label || surface?.name}` in the entry button (and passes `node.label` as a `title` attribute), and `resolveSurface` in `studio-design/navSurface.ts` reads `const label = String(node.label ?? '')` into `Surface.label`. No hunk of the diff falls inside `NavTree`, and `navSurface.ts` is not in the file list, so both are byte-identical at the base: pre-existing, untouched by this PR. A map as a React child throws, which the dev measured through the real `InterfacesPillar` (their uncommitted probe; read-only here, not re-run) — a crash, on a public door, same family as this card.
